s1a: A buyer has opened a PayPal dispute.
s1b: What the shop does next, decides what it costs.
s2a: Answered while it's still a dispute, it costs no PayPal fee.
s2b: Let it become a claim and lose, and the fee is fourteen euros.
s2c: For a busy shop, twenty-eight. Even when the shop wins.
s2e: And disputes cost more than fees: a single customer-care contact, by phone, chat or email, costs about eight dollars.
s2f: Every dollar lost to fraud costs a merchant about four dollars sixty.
s2g: And big merchants give up on almost half of their card chargebacks, and win only one in five of those they fight.
s2h: That's where Second Look comes in. It's an AI that reads every PayPal dispute and the evidence behind it, runs the checks a specialist would, and drafts the answer. Nothing moves until a person approves.
s3a: Meet Linen and Paper, a made-up shop with about two thousand orders a month.
s3b: Marta answers customers, and can give back up to thirty euros on her own. Giulia manages the team.
s4a: Marta opens her helpdesk, a made-up one, for this film.
s4b: Dario has written. Next to his email, Second Look shows his PayPal dispute, already reviewed. Its answer: defend with evidence.
s5a: She opens the case. The courier recorded the apron as delivered three days after it shipped, to the address on Dario's PayPal account.
s5b: Dario has disputed four of his five orders, and took two of them to a claim.
s5c: And she sees what each way out costs: refunding now, twenty-six euros out of pocket; losing a claim, forty.
s6a: She approves. The proof goes to PayPal, the reply goes to Dario, and the ticket records who sent it.
s7a: Next, Pablo. He sent a shirt back, and the refund never went out. He's right.
s7b: But it's eighty-nine euros, over Marta's limit. So the case goes to Giulia, and nothing is sent.
s8a: Giulia sees Marta's note and her reply, and approves the refund.
s8b: Then the overview: what the open cases could cost, and how far the shop is from PayPal's busy-shop line.
s9a: And it runs on PayPal. This is PayPal's sandbox: a one-person shop, a real dispute. The reply went to the buyer, and the tracking went to PayPal as proof.
s10a: The AI recommends. Limits written in code have the last word. A person approves.
